overview.text: Puck, also called Robin Goodfellow, is the mischievous spirit who serves Oberon, king of the fairies, in William Shakespeare’s comedy A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Oberon sends him to use a love-inducing flower, but Puck mistakenly enchants Lysander, helping turn the young Athenians’ romantic confusion into comic chaos. His best-known prank comes when he gives the amateur actor Nick Bottom an ass’s head; the enchanted Queen Titania then falls in love with Bottom. Puck later helps undo the confusion and, in the play’s closing moments, addresses the audience, inviting them to regard the events as a dream. Robin Goodfellow also appears in older folklore, though the early history of that tradition is uncertain.

key_facts.text: Puck serves Oberon and is described in the play as a hobgoblin or “puck.”
Oberon sends Puck to find a flower whose juice makes a person fall in love with the first creature they see.
Puck mistakenly puts the flower’s juice on Lysander’s eyes, adding to the confusion among the four Athenian lovers.
Puck transforms Bottom’s head into that of an ass; Titania, under the flower’s spell, falls in love with him.
The Royal Shakespeare Company notes that a confirmed early reference to Robin Goodfellow appears in 1489, while an earlier possible reference remains uncertain.
